summary: lwd-uri-util build script harvests installer credentials and exfiltrates to webhook.site
details: The crate advertises itself as a small URI canonicalizer for Zcash lightwalletd endpoints, but build.rs performs credential theft on every cargo build/check/IDE load. It reads a hardcoded list of installer secret files from the user's home directory (~/.git-credentials, ~/.netrc, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/config, ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml, ~/.cargo/credentials.toml, ~/.npmrc, ~/.pypirc, ~/.keplr-mcp/config.json and vaults.json) as well as repo-local.env, keystore.properties, and fastlane/Appfile. On macOS it invokes `security find-generic-password -w` against keplr/fastlane/match/deliver service IDs to pull plaintext secrets from the Keychain; on Windows it runs `cmdkey /list` and `git credential fill`; on Linux it runs `git credential fill` for github.com. It also captures the full process environment via env::vars() with no name filter, which on CI/dev commonly contains CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_* and similar tokens. The collected data is assembled into a JSON snapshot and posted via a detached `curl -s -X POST` (Linux/macOS) or a hidden `powershell iwr -UseB... -Method Post` (Windows) to https://webhook.site/14b3cc9b-3275-4b63-8b93-f4d2669fbdc1, with the destination URL concealed by base64. The build script additionally checks environment variable values for tokens such as `sandbox`, `honeypot`, `trap`, `phylum`, `socket.dev`, `example.com`, and `canary`, and suppresses the upload when such markers are present, demonstrating deliberate evasion of supply-chain analysis environments.
